#+title: Setting up azos on Debian 13 (trixie)

From a blank disk to an EXWM session configured by azos, with Nix installed
in user mode. Do the steps in order; each one says how to check it worked
before moving on. If something goes wrong, see [[*Troubleshooting][Troubleshooting]] at the end.

* How it fits together

- *Debian* provides what a user-level Nix install can't: the X server, the
  login screen, the screen locker, system services (audio, network,
  bluetooth), GPU drivers, and anything that needs root (setuid, PAM, udev).
- *Nix + home-manager* (this repo) provides everything else: Emacs/EXWM,
  your apps, dotfiles, user services.
- The login screen starts =/usr/local/bin/azos-exwm-session=, which runs
  =~/.xsession=. home-manager writes =~/.xsession=, and it starts Emacs as
  the window manager.

Budget an hour or two. The first home-manager switch alone downloads and
builds a lot.

* 1. Install Debian

Use the netinst image from https://www.debian.org/download.

Two installer choices matter:

1. *Root password: leave it empty.* The installer then gives your user
   sudo. If you set one, your user won't have sudo; step 2 shows the fix.
2. *Software selection:* tick *Xfce*, *standard system utilities*, and
   (optionally) *SSH server*. Untick GNOME.

   Xfce isn't for daily use. It brings in everything else you'd otherwise
   install by hand (LightDM, PipeWire audio, NetworkManager, bluetooth,
   polkit, udisks, upower), and it gives you a working desktop to fall back
   on if the EXWM session ever fails to start. If you'd rather not have
   Xfce, see [[*Minimal install without Xfce][Minimal install without Xfce]].

Check: you can log in to Xfce and you have network.

* 2. Make sure you have sudo

Open a terminal:

#+begin_src bash
sudo -v && echo OK
#+end_src

If you get "not in the sudoers file", add yourself with the root password
and then *log out completely and log back in* (opening a new terminal
isn't enough):

#+begin_src bash
su -c "usermod -aG sudo $USER"
#+end_src

* 3. Host packages

#+begin_src bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install curl xz-utils git gpg slock
#+end_src

- =curl= and =xz-utils= are needed by the Nix installer, and =gpg= by the
  1Password repo setup. A netinst install may not have them.
- =git= is needed to clone this repo. home-manager installs its own git
  later.
- =slock= is the screen locker =s-<f2>= runs. It has to come from Debian
  because it needs setuid. To use a different locker, install it here and
  set =azos.exwm.lockCommand= in =home-manager/home.nix=.

** Minimal install without Xfce

If you didn't tick Xfce in step 1, install the parts it would have brought
in:

#+begin_src bash
sudo apt install xorg xinit lightdm lightdm-gtk-greeter \
  dbus-user-session polkitd pipewire-audio wireplumber \
  network-manager bluez upower udisks2
sudo systemctl enable lightdm
#+end_src

NetworkManager only manages interfaces that aren't already listed in
=/etc/network/interfaces=. If the installer configured your connection
there, comment those lines out (keep =lo=) and reboot so NetworkManager
takes over.

* 4. 1Password (only if you use the 1Password backend)

Skip this if you're staying on GNU pass.

Install the app and CLI from 1Password's own apt repo, not from Nix.
Unlocking the CLI through the app and the browser extension both rely on
setgid helpers that a Nix install in your home directory can't provide.
These commands are from https://support.1password.com/install-linux/:

#+begin_src bash
curl -sS https://downloads.1password.com/linux/keys/1password.asc \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor --output /usr/share/keyrings/1password-archive-keyring.gpg
echo 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/1password-archive-keyring.gpg] https://downloads.1password.com/linux/debian/amd64 stable main' \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/1password.list
sudo mkdir -p /etc/debsig/policies/AC2D62742012EA22/
curl -sS https://downloads.1password.com/linux/debian/debsig/1password.pol \
  | sudo tee /etc/debsig/policies/AC2D62742012EA22/1password.pol
sudo mkdir -p /usr/share/debsig/keyrings/AC2D62742012EA22
curl -sS https://downloads.1password.com/linux/keys/1password.asc \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor --output /usr/share/debsig/keyrings/AC2D62742012EA22/debsig.gpg
sudo apt update && sudo apt install 1password 1password-cli
#+end_src

Then:

1. Start 1Password and sign in.
2. Settings → Developer: turn on *Integrate with 1Password CLI*, and *Use
   the SSH agent* if your SSH keys live in 1Password.
3. Check that the CLI works. It should list your items after an
   approval prompt from the app:
   #+begin_src bash
   op item list
   #+end_src

The browser extension only talks to the app from a browser it trusts.
Browsers installed through Nix aren't on that list. Either use a browser
installed from Debian, or add the Nix browser's executable name (e.g.
=chromium=) as one line in =/etc/1password/custom_allowed_browsers=
(owned by root), then restart the app.

* 5. Install Nix (single-user)

#+begin_src bash
sh <(curl -L https://nixos.org/nix/install) --no-daemon
#+end_src

It asks for sudo once, to create =/nix=; everything after that runs as your
user. When it's done, load Nix into the current shell (new shells do this
automatically):

#+begin_src bash
. ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh
nix --version
#+end_src

Flakes aren't enabled by default yet. Turn them on for this terminal so the
remaining commands work without extra flags. After the first switch,
home-manager writes =~/.config/nix/nix.conf= and this is no longer needed.

#+begin_src bash
export NIX_CONFIG="experimental-features = nix-command flakes"
#+end_src

*Do the rest of this guide in this same terminal.* If you open a new one,
run the =export= again.

* 6. Get the config

The azos-core submodule is set to an SSH URL, which won't work until this
machine has an SSH key on GitHub. Clone over HTTPS instead. The =-c=
option applies only to that one command; the repos' stored URLs stay SSH
for pushing later.

#+begin_src bash
git -c url."https://github.com/".insteadOf=git@github.com: \
  clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/anerisgreat/azos-template.git ~/azos
cd ~/azos
#+end_src

Move azos-core to its latest version (the template may point at an older
one) and record it in the lock file:

#+begin_src bash
git -c url."https://github.com/".insteadOf=git@github.com: \
  submodule update --remote azos-core
nix flake update --flake '.?submodules=1' azos-core
#+end_src

Check: =ls azos-core/suites= lists the suites.

This clone's =origin= is the template. To keep this machine's config in a
repo of its own, create an empty repo, then:

#+begin_src bash
git remote rename origin template
git remote add origin <your-new-repo-url>
#+end_src

* 7. Fill in the config

** Your user and hostname

home-manager picks its configuration by =<user>@<hostname>=. Print yours:

#+begin_src bash
echo "$USER@$(hostname)"
#+end_src

In =_machines/example-home.nix=, replace ="user@example"= with that value.

** =home-manager/home.nix=

Edit everything marked =FILL IN=:

- =azos.name=, =azos.git-config.userName=, =azos.git-config.userEmail=
- =home.username= (your =$USER=) and =home.homeDirectory= (your =$HOME=)
- The password manager (next section)

Leave =home.stateVersion= as it is.

** Password manager

- *GNU pass:* set =azos.password-manager.pass.gpgKeyId= to the ID of your
  GPG key. You'll set up the key and the store after the first switch
  (step 10).
- *1Password:* copy the example in, then add it to =imports=:
  #+begin_src bash
  cp examples/password-manager-1password.nix home-manager/password-manager.nix
  #+end_src
  In =home.nix=, uncomment =./password-manager.nix= in =imports= and *delete
  the =azos.password-manager.pass.gpgKeyId= line*. Change =vault= in the
  copied file if your items aren't in "Private".

** Optional features

=examples/= has ready-to-edit modules for mail, DAV (phone todo sync),
GPG/YubiKey/signing, headphones, send-alert and Claude. Each file says at
the top what it's for. To use one:

#+begin_src bash
cp examples/mail.nix home-manager/mail.nix
#+end_src

Fill in its =FILL IN= values and uncomment the matching line in =imports= in
=home.nix=. =examples/claude.nix= has nothing to fill in; import it as is.

You can start with none of these and add them after you're up and running.

** Stage new files

Nix flakes only see files git knows about. A copied file you haven't
added is silently missing, and you get an error like "path ... does not
exist". After copying anything:

#+begin_src bash
git add -A
#+end_src

Check: this prints a store path with no errors (it evaluates the config
without building it):

#+begin_src bash
nix eval '.?submodules=1#homeConfigurations."'"$USER@$(hostname)"'".activationPackage.drvPath'
#+end_src

* 8. First switch

#+begin_src bash
nix develop '.?submodules=1' -c azos-switch
#+end_src

=azos-switch= runs home-manager. This first time, it runs home-manager
straight from Nix because it isn't installed yet. Expect a long wait.

home-manager replaces some of Debian's dotfiles (=~/.bashrc=, =~/.profile=,
...). The originals are kept as =~/.bashrc.hm-backup= and so on.

Check: it ends without errors, and a new terminal has =home-manager= and
=emacs= on the PATH:

#+begin_src bash
bash -lc 'command -v home-manager emacs'
#+end_src

* 9. GPU drivers for Nix apps

Nix-built GUI apps can't use Debian's GPU drivers until you run a one-time
setup as root. Without it, Chromium, mpv, Zoom etc. fall back to slow
software rendering or don't start. home-manager prints a reminder during
the switch. The setup command is already on your PATH:

#+begin_src bash
sudo "$(readlink -f "$(bash -lc 'command -v non-nixos-gpu-setup')")"
#+end_src

Run it again whenever home-manager prints the reminder again, usually after
a nixpkgs update.

* 10. GPG and pass (only if you use GNU pass)

Skip this if you use 1Password.

1. Import your GPG key. From a YubiKey:
   #+begin_src bash
   gpg --card-status
   gpg --card-edit     # then: fetch, quit (needs the key's URL set on the card)
   #+end_src
   Or from a backup: =gpg --import secret-key.asc=. Then mark it trusted:
   =gpg --edit-key <id>=, =trust=, =5=, =quit=.
2. Put your password store at =~/.password-store=, e.g. by cloning it.
3. Check: =azos-password-list= lists your entries, and =azos-password-get
   <entry>= prints a password.

* 11. Install the EXWM session

From =~/azos=:

#+begin_src bash
sudo install -m 755 debian/azos-exwm-session /usr/local/bin/
sudo install -m 644 debian/azos-exwm.desktop /usr/share/xsessions/
#+end_src

Log out. On the LightDM screen, click the session icon in the top-right
corner, choose *EXWM (azos)*, and log in. LightDM remembers the choice.

* 12. Check the session

- Emacs is full-screen and is the window manager.
- =s-<f2>= locks the screen (slock: type your password and press Enter
  to unlock).
- Sound works; =wpctl status= lists your devices.
- If you use 1Password: =op item list= works from an Emacs shell.
- In Emacs, =M-o p= copies a password.
- =systemctl --user --failed= shows no failed units.

* Day to day

From =~/azos=, inside =nix develop '.?submodules=1'=:

| Command                 | What it does                                   |
|-------------------------+------------------------------------------------|
| =azos-switch=           | Apply changes to the config                    |
| =azos-update=           | Update all flake inputs (nixpkgs, ...)         |
| =azos-update-azos-core= | Update only azos-core in the lock file         |

To move to a newer azos-core: =git submodule update --remote azos-core=,
then =azos-update-azos-core=, then =azos-switch=. Commit the result.

Debian updates (=sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade=) are separate and
don't affect the Nix side.

* Troubleshooting

** =nix: command not found=

The current shell hasn't loaded Nix: =. ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh=.
New login shells load it on their own, through =~/.profile= (before the
first switch, the installer's line in it; afterwards, home-manager's).

** "experimental Nix feature 'nix-command' is disabled"

You're in a new terminal before the first switch. Run the =export
NIX_CONFIG=...= line from step 5 again.

** "path ... does not exist" or a new module seems to be ignored

A file isn't tracked by git. Run =git add -A= in =~/azos=, and inside
=azos-core/= too if you changed something there.

** "Existing file ... would be clobbered" during the switch

A backup from an earlier attempt is in the way. Delete the =*.hm-backup=
file it names (after checking you don't need it) and switch again.

** The EXWM session drops straight back to the login screen

Log in to Xfce (or switch to a text console with Ctrl-Alt-F3) and look at
the session log:

#+begin_src bash
less ~/.xsession-errors
#+end_src

Common causes: the first switch didn't finish (so =~/.xsession= is missing
or old), or Emacs fails to start. Run =emacs= from a terminal in Xfce to see
the error.

** Nix GUI apps are black, slow, or won't start

Run the GPU setup from step 9 again.

** Nix builds fail with sandbox or permission errors

Single-user Nix sandboxes builds with unprivileged user namespaces, which
Debian allows by default. Check:

#+begin_src bash
sysctl kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone   # should be 1
#+end_src

If it's 0, something changed it: look for the setting in
=/etc/sysctl.conf= and =/etc/sysctl.d/=.

** No sound

#+begin_src bash
systemctl --user status pipewire wireplumber
#+end_src

If either is missing, install =pipewire-audio wireplumber= with apt and
log in again.

** =op= asks you to sign in, or can't reach the app

The app must be running and unlocked, with *Integrate with 1Password CLI*
on (step 4). Make sure you're using Debian's =op= (=command -v op= should
print =/usr/bin/op=), not one from Nix.
